newsitem.title: CHINA: China 2000 soybean output seen up 25 pct from '94.
newsitem.headline: China 2000 soybean output seen up 25 pct from '94.

text.p: China's soybean output is forecast to climb by 25 percent to 20 million tonnes in the year 2000 compared with 1994, the Futures Herald said in an edition seen in Beijing on Friday.
But whether the target could be achieved hinged on soybean prices, said the Wednesday edition of the newspaper based in the central province of Henan.

Many farmers preferred to plant corn over soybeans because corn output per hectare (acre) of land was higher than that of soybeans, it quoted agricultural expert Lu Ming as saying, adding that corn prices were rising.
Only when soybean prices were 300 times that of corn would farmers be willing to plant soybeans, the newspaper said.
Land under soybean in 1994 totalled 9.2 million hectares (22.7 million acres), it said, quoting the latest official figures.
